newsitem.title: INDIA: India to spend $4.19 billion to boost employment.
newsitem.headline: India to spend $4.19 billion to boost employment.

text.p: India plans to help up to two million youths in self-employment ventures in a bid to generate five million jobs over the next five years, Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Tuesday.
"With enhanced enterprise financing, this would mean an outlay from the banking sector to the tune of 150 billion rupees ($4.19 billion)", he said.
"The subsidy portion alone will be 15 billion rupees," he added.
Maran, speaking at a conference to review employment generating schemes across India, said the move was expected to generate nearly four to five million jobs within the next five years.
In 1993 India launched an employment scheme to help 700,000 educated unemployed youths to set up enterprises, a government statement said on Tuesday.
The scheme was expected to generate employment for about 1.4 million people.
India's total unemployed is estimated at around 37 million in a population of 936 million, according to latest government projections.
